title: The Year Hollywood Changed the National Security Debate
gist: Zelizer argues that 1983's WarGames and The Day After shifted U.S. national security policy — prompting Reagan's computer-security directive NSDD-145 and contributing to his turn toward arms control — and that the new documentary The AI Doc aims to do the same for AI regulation. Popular culture remains one of the few spaces able to move a public that distrusts institutions, making it a lever for AI policy.

themes.theme: Culture as a lever for AI regulation

insights.claim: The documentary The AI Doc: Or How I Became An Apocaloptimist, modeled on 1983's The Day After per Center for Humane Technology co-founder Tristan Harris, aims to alarm broad audiences about unchecked AI development and was screened for members of Congress and staff last month.
insights.speaker: Julian E. Zelizer
insights.so_what: AI-safety advocates are taking their case directly to lawmakers via mass culture, raising the odds of U.S. AI regulation.
insights.quote: an example of the power that a film can have to nudge the world in a different direction.

themes.theme: The Day After and Reagan's arms-control turn

insights.claim: The Day After, aired by ABC on Nov. 20, 1983, was seen by over 100 million people, jammed White House phone lines, and left Reagan 'greatly depressed' by his own diary account.
insights.speaker: Julian E. Zelizer
insights.so_what: Shows the scale of public reaction a single broadcast once achieved.
insights.quote: it’s very effective and left me greatly depressed.

insights.claim: The Day After was part of the public pressure that moved Reagan from confrontation toward 'peace' — leading to 1985-87 summits with Gorbachev and the INF Treaty eliminating an entire class of missiles — though many factors contributed, including his belief in nuclear abolition.
insights.speaker: Julian E. Zelizer
insights.so_what: Public fear can shift even hawkish administrations toward negotiated limits on dangerous technologies.

insights.claim: 1983 saw peak superpower tension — the Soviet shootdown of a South Korean airliner and NATO's Able Archer 83 exercise, which some Soviet officials feared was cover for a real attack, prompting Soviet air units onto high alert.
insights.speaker: Julian E. Zelizer
insights.so_what: Context for how close miscalculation came; relevant analog for AI-in-command-and-control risks.
